title: Graphing a Downward-Shifted Inverse-Square Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Analyze and describe the graph of y = 1/x^2 - 1 by identifying its parent function, shift, asymptotes, domain, range, and intercepts.

steps.title: Identify the Parent Function and Vertical Shift
steps.explanation: Subtracting 1 from the parent function y = 1/x^2 shifts its graph 1 unit downward.
steps.why: Subtracting 1 translates every point on y = 1/x^2 vertically downward by 1 unit.

steps.title: Determine the Asymptotes, Domain, and Range
steps.explanation: The vertical asymptote is the y-axis x = 0, and the horizontal asymptote shifts down to y = -1. Since 1/x^2 > 0 for all x != 0, we have 1/x^2 - 1 > -1, so the range is (-1, infinity).
steps.why: Shifting the range (0, infinity) of 1/x^2 down by 1 produces (-1, infinity).

steps.title: Locate the x-Intercepts
steps.explanation: The even graph is symmetric about the y-axis, crossing the x-axis at (-1, 0) and (1, 0) and approaching y = -1 from above as x -> +/-infinity.
